title: Normalized constant towers and the actual strict quotient-augmentation square
statement:
Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Fix a Noetherian adic datum $(A,I)$, put $P_n=A/I^n$ and $B_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ for $T=X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $c_g:g^{-1}B_X\to B_Y$ be the projection-defined coefficient map and $G(M)=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}B_X,c_g}B_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Let $F:\operatorname{Mod}(B_X)\to\operatorname{Mod}(B_Y)$ be additive exact and $m:G\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ a specified natural isomorphism. Use module sheaves, unbounded derived categories with localizations $Q_X,Q_Y$, and strict inverse sequences [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-inverse-system]. Let $(L,\epsilon),(\widetilde L,\tau)$ be specified universal left-derived pairs for ordinary and levelwise $G$, computed on objectwise K-flat flat-term complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. Let $F_D,F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ be exact termwise descents, with localization comparisons $\xi,\Xi$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Suppose natural isomorphisms $e:L\to F_D$, $E:\widetilde L\to F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ satisfy $\xi_Pe_{Q_XP}=Q_Y(m_P)\epsilon_P$ and $\Xi_ME_{Q_X^{\mathrm{Tow}}M}=Q_Y^{\mathrm{Tow}}(m_M^{\mathrm{Tow}})\tau_M$ for all complexes $P,M$.

Let $\Delta_T$ denote the exact constant-tower functors and their derived descents. Let $b:\Delta_YL\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde L\Delta_X$ be the counit-normalized comparison of [lem-cbc-derived-constant-tower-normalization] for $G$, characterized on K-flat flat-term $P$ by $\tau_{\Delta_XP}b_{Q_XP}=\Delta_Y(\epsilon_P)$. Let $c:\Delta_YF_D\xrightarrow{\sim}F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}\Delta_X$ be induced by the identity on complexes $\Delta_YF=F^{\mathrm{Tow}}\Delta_X$ using exact localization. Then, for every unbounded $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$,
$$E_{\Delta_XK}b_K=c_K\Delta_Y(e_K).$$

Choose a K-flat flat-term representative $P$ of $K$, put $R(P)_n=P\otimes_{B_X}(P_n)_X$, with its actual quotient transitions, and $a_P:\Delta_XP\to R(P)$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Let $K_\bullet=Q_X^{\mathrm{Tow}}R(P)$ and $a_K:\Delta_XK\to K_\bullet$ be the localized augmentation. The actual strict pulled-back augmentation represented by $w_P=\widetilde L(Q_X^{\mathrm{Tow}}a_P)\tau_{\Delta_XP}^{-1}$, after identifying $LK$ with $Q_YG(P)$ by $\epsilon_P$, is
$$\beta_K=\widetilde L(a_K)b_K:\Delta_YLK\to\widetilde L K_\bullet.$$
The corresponding exact augmentation is $\beta^F_K=F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}(a_K)c_K$. These identifications are independent of the chosen K-flat representatives and of strict resolutions of $R(P)$, and
$$E_{K_\bullet}\beta_K=\beta^F_K\Delta_Y(e_K).$$
This is equality of morphisms in the derived strict-tower category, with the specified augmentations. No K-flatness of the quotient levels and no intrinsic completeness of $K$ are assumed.

proof.text:
Use the canonical exact-localization identifications throughout. Put $b'_K=E_{\Delta_XK}^{-1}c_K\Delta_Y(e_K)$. This is a natural isomorphism. The identity on complexes defining $c$ gives $\Xi_{\Delta_XP}c_{Q_XP}=\Delta_Y(\xi_P)$ by the natural-transformation lifting clause of localization. Put $M_P=Q_Y^{\mathrm{Tow}}(m^{\mathrm{Tow}}_{\Delta_XP})=\Delta_YQ_Y(m_P)$. The two assumed counit equations imply
$$M_P\tau_{\Delta_XP}b'_{Q_XP}=\Xi_{\Delta_XP}E_{\Delta_XQ_XP}b'_{Q_XP}=\Delta_Y(\xi_Pe_{Q_XP})=M_P\Delta_Y(\epsilon_P).$$
Cancel the isomorphism $M_P$. On K-flat flat-term $P$ this is exactly the normalization characterizing $b$. Uniqueness in the constant-tower normalization lemma yields $b'=b$, hence $E_{\Delta_XK}b_K=c_K\Delta_Y(e_K)$ for every $K$.

proof.text:
Apply the strict quotient-pullback computation to $g$, $B_X,B_Y$ and the specified tower pair. It identifies the actual resolved augmentation with $w_P=\widetilde L(Q_X^{\mathrm{Tow}}a_P)\tau_{\Delta_XP}^{-1}$, with the actual quotient transitions. The constant-tower normalization gives $b_{Q_XP}=\tau_{\Delta_XP}^{-1}\Delta_Y(\epsilon_P)$. Therefore the augmentation with source $\Delta_YLK$ is
$$w_P\Delta_Y(\epsilon_P)=\widetilde L(a_K)\tau_{\Delta_XP}^{-1}\Delta_Y(\epsilon_P)=\widetilde L(a_K)b_K=\beta_K.$$
Exact termwise descent computes the exact augmentation without a resolution: applying $F$ to $a_P$ and the identity constant-tower comparison gives $\beta^F_K=F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}(a_K)c_K$.

proof.text:
Naturality of the specified transformation $E$ at the morphism $a_K:\Delta_XK\to K_\bullet$ gives
$$E_{K_\bullet}\beta_K=E_{K_\bullet}\widetilde L(a_K)b_K=F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}(a_K)E_{\Delta_XK}b_K=F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}(a_K)c_K\Delta_Y(e_K)=\beta^F_K\Delta_Y(e_K).$$
The second equality is naturality, the third is Step 1, and the last is Step 2. This computation takes place in the derived category of strict towers itself.

proof.text: For a strict resolving arrow $r:H_\bullet\to R(P)$, the quotient-pullback lemma supplies $\chi_r=\tau_{H_\bullet}\widetilde L(Q_X^{\mathrm{Tow}}r)^{-1}$. It identifies the actual augmentation with $\chi_rw_P$; for another $s$, the canonical comparison $\chi_s\chi_r^{-1}$ identifies these arrows and satisfies the cocycle. Thus no inverse of $\tau_{R(P)}$ or lift of $a_P$ is needed. For representative independence, the strict coefficient-augmentation lemma says $R(f)a_P=a_{P'}\Delta_Xf$ and both $R(f)$ and $\Delta_Xf$ are quasi-isomorphisms when $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat flat-term representatives. The quotient-pullback lemma makes $w$ natural for these maps, so cancellation of their localized isomorphisms identifies the augmented arrows. For arbitrary resolutions $P\to M$ and $P'\to M$, the right Ore square for quasi-isomorphisms in the homotopy category gives a common source mapping to $P,P'$ by quasi-isomorphisms (two-out-of-three). Replace that source by a K-flat flat-term complex using the diagram replacement theorem with the one-object index category. The resulting two maps are represented by chain maps, and the preceding naturality equalities apply on both legs. Exact descent also inverts these arrows. Consequently the two computed augmentations, $b$ and the displayed square agree under the canonical derived identifications, independently of both choices. No step imposes flatness on the quotients or intrinsic completeness on $K$.
